compounddef.title: BVH2D Spatial Indexing for Path SDF Computation

detaileddescription.para: This document records the performance investigation and implementation findings for accelerating 2D Path Signed Distance Field (SDF) evaluation using a Bounding Volume Hierarchy (BVH2D).

sect1.title: 1. Context and Motivation
sect1.para: Computing the distance field of a 2D polyline or polygon across a discrete heightmap grid is a recurring operation in terrain authoring, hydrology (riverbed carve profiles), and carving workflows.

The original evaluation in path_sdf_to_array and sdf_2d_polyline performed brute-force distance evaluation:
For every pixel $(i, j)$ in a $W \times H$ array, iterate across all $N$ path segments.
Complexity: $\mathcal{O}(W \cdot H \cdot N)$.
For dense or detailed paths ($N \ge 100$) and high-resolution heightmaps ($512 \times 512$ or higher), this approach causes significant CPU bottlenecks.
HighMap provides an internal 2D Axis-Aligned Bounding Box tree (hmap::BVH2D). By indexing the segment set into a BVH, the nearest segment search per pixel is accelerated via branch-and-bound pruning.

sect2.title: Segment Indexing
sect2.para: Path segments $[p_k, p_{k+1}]$ are packaged into Segment2D structs storing directional vector $d = p_{k+1} - p_k$ and inverse squared length $\frac{1}{|d|^2}$. A BVH2D tree is built over the segments in $\mathcal{O}(N \log N)$ time.

sect2.title: Branch-and-Bound Distance Query
sect2.para:
For a given query point $p = (x, y)$:
Traverse the BVH using a fixed-capacity traversal stack.
At each node, compute the minimum squared distance from $p$ to the node's axis-aligned bounding box (AABB2D): $$d_{\text{box}}^2(p, \text{box}) = \max(0, \text{box.min}_x - p_x, p_x - \text{box.max}_x)^2 + \max(0, \text{box.min}_y - p_y, p_y - \text{box.max}_y)^2$$
If $d_{\text{box}}^2 \ge d_{\text{best}}^2$, the node and all its descendants are pruned.
For internal nodes, visit the closer child first to tighten $d_{\text{best}}^2$ quickly.
In leaf nodes, evaluate exact point-to-segment distance squared and update $d_{\text{best}}^2$.
Average per-query complexity drops to $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$, reducing overall runtime to $\mathcal{O}(W \cdot H \log N)$.

sect2.title: Support for Domain Warping and Path Closure

listitem.para: Domain Warping: Per-pixel noise displacements (p_noise_x, p_noise_y) warp coordinate $p = (x + dx, y + dy)$ before querying the tree. The tree does not require reconstruction.
Closed Paths: When path.is_closed() == true, the closing segment is included in the BVH, and an orientation/winding sign test determines interior vs. exterior distances.

sect1.title: 3. Benchmark Measurements
sect1.para: Google Benchmark was executed comparing the baseline brute-force approach against the BVH approach on a CPU with 6 physical cores (12 threads).

sect1.title: 4. API Design and Integration
sect1.para: The functionality is structured to preserve backward compatibility while providing the brute-force implementation for reference and validation:

listitem.para:
Explicit Implementations:
hmap::sdf_2d_polyline_bvh and hmap::path_sdf_to_array_bvh
hmap::sdf_2d_polyline_brute_force and hmap::path_sdf_to_array_brute_force

Default Wrapper Functions:
hmap::sdf_2d_polyline(path, shape, bbox, p_noise_x, p_noise_y, use_bvh = true)
hmap::path_sdf_to_array(path, shape, bbox_array, p_noise_x, p_noise_y, use_bvh = true)

sect1.para: Existing call sites retain default use_bvh = true behavior without signature breakage.

sect1.title: 5. Verification of Bézier Polyline SDF (<tt>sdf_2d_polyline_bezier</tt>)
sect1.para: During verification of sdf_2d_polyline_bezier, numerical issues were discovered causing corrupted/broken results (entire arrays returning NaN or inf).

listitem.para: Division by Zero on Colinear/Degenerate Segments: The distance to a quadratic Bézier curve $B(t) = (1-t)^2 P_0 + 2t(1-t)P_1 + t^2 P_2$ involves the second-difference vector: $$b = P_0 - 2P_1 + P_2$$ When the control points are colinear (or $P_1$ is at the midpoint of $P_0$ and $P_2$), $b \approx 0 \implies \text{dot}(b, b) = 0$. The original code computed: floatkk=1.0f/dot(b,b); without checking for zero. This produced inf, which cascaded through Cardano's cubic solver into NaN for all grid queries. Fix: When $\text{dot}(b, b) < 10^{-10}$, the curve degenerates to a straight line segment $[P_0, P_2]$. The solver directly evaluates the point-to-line-segment distance.

Domain Violations in Trigonometric Cardano Branch: For the 3-real-roots case ($h < 0$ in the cubic discriminant), the solution evaluates: floatv=std::acos(q/(p*zz*2.0f))/3.0f; Due to float32 precision limits, $\frac{q}{2 p z}$ occasionally evaluated to $1.0000002$ or $-1.0000002$, triggering domain errors in std::acos and returning NaN. Fix: Clamped the ratio to $[-1.0f, 1.0f]$ via std::clamp.

Topology and Point Count Handling: Quadratic Bézier paths are indexed as triplets $(P_{2k}, P_{2k+1}, P_{2k+2})$. Paths with an even number of points previously appended a synthetic point that was frequently colinear with the last segment, triggering the division by zero. Proper segment pairing was enforced.

sect2.title: BVH2D Acceleration for Bézier Curves
sect2.para: Since quadratic Bézier curves satisfy the convex hull property: $$B(t) \in \text{ConvexHull}(P_0, P_1, P_2) \quad \forall t \in [0, 1]$$ A tight and conservative bounding box for each quadratic curve is simply: $$\text{AABB} = [\min(P_0, P_1, P_2), \max(P_0, P_1, P_2)]$$
A specialized BVH2DBezier tree was implemented using this bounding box representation. Per-pixel queries prune subtrees whose bounding box distance exceeds the current closest squared distance.

The API was structured consistently with linear polyline SDF:
hmap::sdf_2d_polyline_bezier_bvh
hmap::sdf_2d_polyline_bezier_brute_force
hmap::sdf_2d_polyline_bezier(path, shape, bbox, p_noise_x, p_noise_y, use_bvh = true)

sect1.title: 6. GPU (OpenCL) Assessment and Validation
sect1.para: The GPU polyline SDF implementation was analyzed to determine whether introducing a BVH2D spatial index in OpenCL kernels would yield benefits.

sect2.title: Rationale: Keeping the GPU Kernel Brute Force
sect2.para: Building and traversing a BVH2D on the GPU was rejected based on execution characteristics:

listitem.para:
Constant Memory Broadcast Efficiency: Path vertices are placed in __constant float* (or read-only global cache lines). During execution, all 32 threads in an execution warp evaluate the identical segment index simultaneously:
Warp broadcast achieves a 100% cache hit rate with zero memory latency penalty.
Brute-force loop execution exhibits zero warp divergence.

Warp Divergence in BVH Traversal: Neighboring pixels traverse different branches of a BVH depending on their spatial coordinates. Per-warp branch divergence on a tree traversal serializes execution threads and requires a per-work-item stack (causing register pressure or spilling into high-latency local/private memory).

Performance Trade-Off: At $N = 1000$ segments, the brute-force GPU kernel takes only 5.6 ms. The complexity of dynamic tree traversal in OpenCL would likely degrade throughput rather than improve it for typical path sizes.

sect2.title: Numerical Stability and Parity Fixes on GPU
sect2.para: The OpenCL kernels were reviewed and aligned with the CPU implementations:

listitem.para: Colinear Bézier Segments: In HighMap/src/gpu_opencl/kernels/transform/sdf_2d_polyline.cl, added a check for $b_len_sq = \text{dot}(b, b) < 10^{-10}\text{f}$. When degenerate, the kernel falls back to line segment distance between endpoints, preventing division-by-zero inf and NaN cascades.
Cardano Root Solver Clamping: Clamped acos argument to $[-1.0\text{f}, 1.0\text{f}]$ within the 3-real-roots cubic solver branch to avoid domain errors from float rounding.

Closed Path Signing and Topology:
gpu::sdf_2d_polyline_bezier now appends the closing segment to reconnect the first and last control points when path.is_closed() == true.
The kernel takes an is_closed parameter and computes ray-crossing parity to assign interior negative signs, matching the CPU signed distance field behavior.
